current.text: Julius Randle joined Brooklyn. He is a ball-dominant player at Porter's position, so Porter will play more at small forward.
Porter is a projected Brooklyn starter, next to Mikel Brown Jr., Egor Demin, Julius Randle and Day'Ron Sharpe.
His usage is expected to drop because Randle, Brown and a second-year Demin will take more of the ball.
He may lose some three-point volume. His 36.2% from three was the lowest among the top six in threes made.
Josh Minott and Noah Clowney may also take some of his minutes.
He becomes an unrestricted free agent next summer and has no extension. The Nets do not seem to see him as a long-term piece.
A trade during the season is very possible, most likely if he and the team do not agree on an extension. One expert expects it within six months.

Experts disagree on how much a trade would hurt. One expert says it could cut his usage and drop him to around the 90th best player. The newest call says he would not fall far below pick 60 even if traded.
Experts disagree on his production. Some expect him to be clearly worse than last season. The newest call says he can keep up last season's per-game level.

Experts see him as good value around pick 60 or in round 6. One expert ranks him 45 to 60 in category leagues and says the market has priced in his new situation fairly. His worst case is around 75th.
ESPN's rank of 42 is too high for him with Randle on the team.
Brooklyn does not own its draft pick, which goes to Houston, so the team has little reason to tank or rest him.
He may play more games than last season. March minutes are still uncertain because Brooklyn has little to play for and may give minutes to young players.
He ended last season with a hamstring injury and is not injured now.
There is no major health concern going into the season.
Brooklyn has 16 back-to-backs, tied with Boston for the most in the league. In our playoff weeks 19 to 21 the Nets play 3-4-3, which is 10 games with one back-to-back.
Brooklyn is projected to be one of the worst teams, with about 28 wins.

durable.text: He gives points, a lot of threes and good rebounds. He makes many threes for a forward.
He gives little in assists and blocks, and he does not get to the rim much.
His fantasy value comes from efficiency and high usage. It drops if his role shrinks.
His FT% has changed a lot from season to season: 84%, then 76%, then a career-best 86%.
He has a long injury history. It includes a hamstring injury late last season and injury concerns earlier in his career.

note: Experts value him around pick 60 or round 6. Yahoo values him at 17 USD but managers there pay only 4.1 USD on average, while ESPN pays 11.0 USD and our league paid 10 USD last season, so a price of about 10 to 15 USD looks fair for a 3PM, PTS and FT% forward. He fits builds that give up assists or blocks, but on 16 to 18 shots a game his FG% and turnovers are not a help. Early in the season, check how much usage he keeps next to Randle, watch for trade news before the 2027-03-04 deadline, and remember that Brooklyn's 10-game playoff schedule is light.
